bullets.title: AI capex sustainability hinges on $400-600B ARR threshold by end-2027
bullets.body: Multiple research desks (22V, JPM, GS) converge on a critical threshold: frontier AI labs need $400-600B in annualized revenue exiting 2027 to justify 2029+ capex plans, with a path to ~$1T by 2028-29. OpenAI's September ARR came in at ~$50B (later clarified as on track to reach $70B by year-end), triggering mid-week semi/AI selling before stabilizing. Anthropic IPO is flagged as the next key disclosure event for AI lab ARR transparency.

bullets.title: Fed signals more hikes ahead; Waller most hawkish in years
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller reversed his prior dovish stance, explicitly calling for additional rate hikes in December and March to achieve 2% inflation. FOMC minutes showed majority see strengthened labor markets. S&P input costs rose fastest in nearly 4 years; energy, AI capex, and war cited as inflation risk factors. October hike odds collapsed from ~64% to ~22% on stable recent data, but the hiking direction is intact.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury at 5.25-5.35%; secular bond bear market intact; 30-year at 24-year high
bullets.body: 10-year yields reached cycle highs around 5.25-5.35% with 22V targeting 6% and 30-year targeting 8%. Bond market stress is elevated (MOVE near April 2025 dysfunction levels) while equities remain resilient near record highs—an unusual divergence. Hyperscaler bond issuance (MSFT, META, AMZN, GOOGL, ORCL) now represents 14% of net new Treasury supply, concentrated at 30yr+ maturities, adding term-premium pressure.

bullets.title: S&P breadth near historic lows despite index near records; 75-80% of stocks down since mid-August
bullets.body: S&P 500 near all-time highs but only ~25-30% of constituents outperformed (2nd percentile breadth since 2005). Russell 2000 down for five straight weeks, down ~9% from cycle peak. NYSE new lows outnumbered new highs 85% of sessions since August 14. Tech/AI concentration (top 5 stocks ~30% of index) is masking deteriorating internals. Equal-weight S&P triggered MACD buy signal and had its first positive week in eight weeks in the digest window.

bullets.title: AI trade rotating: Software outperforming Semis by ~800bps; 'inference economy' names bid
bullets.body: Software (IGV +3.9%) sharply outperformed semis (SOX -4.3%) on the week. Inference-economy names (SNOW, CRWD, NET, PLTR) were bid even amid semi weakness, trading on lower capex beta and deployment thesis. Mag7 outperformed QQQ for 8 of last 10 weeks. Heavy HF selling of semis continued (-1.5z in North America), while large-cap banks were bought for second straight week. The market is rotating from AI hardware into AI software/deployment.

bullets.title: SpaceX acquires 800MHz low-band spectrum for ~$8B, threatening T/VZ/TMUS, lifting towers
bullets.body: SpaceX acquired 14MHz of 800MHz low-band spectrum from Grain Management for ~$6-8B, enabling satellite-terrestrial hybrid mobile network and direct-to-device coverage. T, VZ, and TMUS dropped 9-12% on spectrum announcement and bearish options surged. Tower stocks (AMT, CCI, SBAC) rallied 3-18% on expectation SpaceX needs 60-70K macro sites. MS models <1% US mobile penetration by 2030, scaling to ~7% by 2035, primarily rural initially. FCC already approved 15,000 next-gen satellites.

bullets.title: MRVL Investor Day raises FY28 to $20B, targets $70-90B by FY31 on AI connectivity strength
bullets.body: Marvell raised FY28 revenue guidance from ~$18B to ~$20B and introduced a FY31 target of $70-90B (55-60% CAGR), with custom XPU revenue reaching ~$30B and interconnect ~$37.5B. Stock rallied 5-8% during the event. Street upgraded with consensus PTs averaging ~$337 (+13%). Optical/comms names (CIEN +13.8%, ALAB +7.6%, MTSI +6.8%) surged on interconnect commentary. UBS, JPM, Wolfe all raised targets significantly.

bullets.title: TSMC September revenue +55% YoY; capex expectations raised to $85B/$98B for 2027/2028
bullets.body: TSMC printed record Q3 revenues (NT$1.49tn, +51-55% YoY) beating expectations on AI chip demand and Blackwell ramp. GS raised 2027-28 capex forecasts to $85B/$98B. TSMC is also exploring a potential second US fab cluster in Texas that could exceed $265B total investment. Key focus at upcoming earnings: gross margin stability into N2 ramp, 2027+ capex, and GenAI supply/demand visibility. TSMC exploring potential partnership with Tesla/SpaceX for dedicated capacity.

bullets.title: Semiconductor cycle likely peaking Q4-26; analog deeply underperforming; memory out of favor
bullets.body: Evercore supply chain checks show lead times past 40 weeks and double ordering inflecting—classic late-cycle signals. Analog semis underperforming ISM relationship by the most since mid-August. Memory (DRAM) down 7.4% on the week. AAPL cut iPhone 18 Pro component orders ~15% on soft demand. PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY in Q3 to 62.7M units (HP -30.9%, Dell -25%). Semi P/E compression expected 3-6 months ahead of earnings peak, consistent with historical analog/MCU pattern.

bullets.title: Meta Muse agent disrupts travel/OTA/retail; marketplace selloff seen as 'overdone'
bullets.body: Meta's Muse ranked #1 US App Store for 22 consecutive days, with 6.6M+ downloads and 1.8M DAUs. OTA stocks (EXPE, BKNG, ABNB) fell 15-25% on fears agents bypass OTA intermediaries. Wolfe and Citi both conclude marketplace selloff fears appear overdone—only 27% of consumers have tried Muse and 64% won't trust agents with credit cards. Amazon blocked Muse from its platform. Hotels are positioned as net beneficiaries while OTAs face commission pool pressure.

bullets.title: French fiscal crisis: OAT-Bund spreads >150bp; ECB TPI threshold very high
bullets.body: French 30yr OAT-Bund spreads exceeded 150bp (above eurozone debt crisis 2010s levels at ~130bp) on structural fiscal challenges. France's deficit expected at 5.4% of GDP in 2027 vs 5.0% government target, and debt stabilization would require ~2% primary surplus—a 5pp turnaround. ECB TPI intervention bar remains very high; possible responses include temporary QT pause or reinvestment tilting. French political system cannot address fiscal challenges until May 2027 elections. Italian BTPs facing contagion.

bullets.title: 3Q26 earnings season: 29.5% EPS growth expected, strongest pre-season bar since 2021
bullets.body: Consensus S&P 500 EPS growth of 29.5% YoY in Q3, with AI infrastructure spending accounting for ~50% of that growth. Record number of positive pre-announcements. TSMC's +55% September revenue confirmed AI investment thesis is intact. All 11 sectors expected positive revenue and EPS growth. Goldman estimates median S&P 500 stock earnings growth of 9% in Q3 (down from 14% in Q2), with Mag7 contributing ~25pp of total index growth. Large bank earnings kick off next week (C, GS, JPM, WFC on Oct 13).

bullets.title: AI power demand real and contracting: GOOGL-CEG 890MW nuclear deal; data center moratoriums rising
bullets.body: Google signed a 20-year 890MW nuclear deal with Constellation plus 2.7GW existing capacity PPA. CEG rallied ~12-16%. IPPs (CEG, VST, TLN) surging ~15% on average on the week as power demand is increasingly viewed as real and monetizable. Simultaneously, data center project cancellations exceeded $200B as San Francisco, Oakland, Raleigh, and other cities imposed moratoriums. Goldman estimates 34% net US power shortfall through 2028. Morgan Stanley forecasts ~120GW ($240B) behind-the-meter power TAM through 2029.

bullets.title: Lumentum optical sold out through early 2029; 70% demand unmet; OCP conference key watch
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO confirmed optical components for AI servers are completely sold out through early 2029, extending the prior 2028 sell-out timeline by six months. Company cannot meet ~70% of demand for some products through next year. LITE surged +567% YTD. OCP Global Summit (Oct 12-15) is the key near-term catalyst for 1.6T optics, 800V power, and NVLink Fusion expansion. MRVL's interconnect commentary sparked sympathy gains across the optical ecosystem.

bullets.title: Amazon in talks to acquire AI startup Decart for ~$7B; AI M&A scramble intensifies
bullets.body: Amazon is in discussions to acquire Decart AI startup for ~$7B. Decart had previously been in talks with Nvidia (which moved on after higher offers) and Anthropic (which ended pursuit as of Sept 7). Decart raised $300M at ~$4B valuation three months prior. Separately, SpaceX seeking $40B to purchase Nvidia chips via Apollo-led deal, and Nvidia in talks to acquire/invest in Reflection AI via potential 'acqui-hire'. Broadcom arranging $50B+ financing for OpenAI's custom chip buildout.

bullets.title: Employment upturn early cycle, tech mid-cycle; nominal GDP at 6.3% YoY—strongest in 41 years
bullets.body: PSC Macro's Nancy Lazar sees employment upturn in goods-producing jobs (6x employment multiplier) set to accelerate through 2027. Nominal GDP growth at 6.3% YoY, strongest in 41+ years, with 3Q EPS tracking 29.6% growth. Tech capex expected 35-50% YoY in 2027 vs FactSet's 18% estimate. Consumer sentiment at 20+ year lows per GS/Michigan surveys, but consumer spending holding at ~4% driven by higher gas station spend and K-shaped economy with household liquidity concentrated in top 20% of earners.

bullets.title: HF positioning: Semis most net sold globally; banks bought for second week; EU vs US gap stretched
bullets.body: Goldman Prime: Info Tech most net sold sector in North America (-1.0 SDs) after being most net bought in 4 of prior 5 weeks. Hedge funds bought US large-cap banks for second straight week as market expects 4Q rebound. EU positioning fell to 13th percentile vs US at 46th percentile—stretched gap. Overall book gross leverage at 308.7% (60th percentile 1yr) and net leverage at 75.9% (10th percentile, historically low). Quant funds slightly positive after strong September.

bullets.title: China AI revenue ~10% of OpenAI/Anthropic combined; DeepSeek V4 first on Huawei Ascend
bullets.body: China's six leading AI firms collectively earn ~10% of OpenAI and Anthropic combined in AI-related revenue. DeepSeek's V4 is the first major model built on Huawei's Ascend chips; DeepSeek open-sourced tools to reduce Nvidia CUDA lock-in. China aggressively stockpiling DUVi lithography systems from ASML. Congressional push for MATCH Act DUVi ban on China attached to Senate NDAA—fate uncertain. Tencent signed a reported $7B deal to rent advanced compute from Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Democrats ~65% favored for Senate, >90% for House; market implications modest
bullets.body: Prediction markets price Democrats at ~65% for Senate, >90% to net 3+ House seats. Base case 50-50 to 51-49D Senate. Andy's (Piper) odds of Democratic sweep raised to 55% from 45%. Historical precedent: 10-year yields typically peak after midterm elections (similar to 2018/2022). Wolfe takes the 'under' on Democratic Senate odds, citing structural challenges in Trump+11 states. Divided government likely limits significant policy changes regardless of specific outcome.

bullets.title: Global PMI at 4-year high; goods inflation set to jump sharply; Euro area GDP cut to 1%
bullets.body: Global composite PMI rose to highest level in four years, consistent with ~3.3% annualized global growth. Global goods inflation set to jump sharply as energy, food, and core all rising; headline CPI expected firm at 0.55% with core soft at 0.18%. Euro area 3Q GDP marked down to 1% annualized (Germany cut to 0.25%, France to 0.5%). German factory orders fell 10.6% in August. EM Asia broadening tightening cycle; RBI delivered expected 25bp hike with 'calibrated tightening' signal.
